incumbent.name: Bob Morris
incumbent.summary: Bob Morris, a Fort Wayne small-business owner, has represented House District 84 since 2010 and chairs the House Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development Committee {caucus_morris}. In 2026 he filed a bill to require that execution teams be made up of volunteer legislators, saying he opposes the death penalty {caucus_hb1287}.
record: Committees: Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development (chair); Employment, Labor and Pensions; Utilities, Energy and Telecommunications, according to the House Republican caucus {caucus_morris}.

2026: Filed HB 1287, requiring the state prison warden to select an execution team only from General Assembly members who volunteer, with their names public {caucus_hb1287}. Morris said, "Don't give anyone a job that you wouldn't want to do yourself" {caucus_hb1287}. WANE reported he came out against the death penalty in 2024 and that his earlier repeal bill, HB 1030, received no committee hearing {wane_hb1287}.
2026: Co-authored HEA 1424, described by the caucus as supporting farmers and small businesses {caucus_newlaws}.

Voted yes on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (April 10, 2025) {rc_sea1_433} and HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill (Dec. 5, 2025) {rc_hb1032_28}. Was recorded as excused on the April 25, 2025 vote adopting the HEA 1001 budget conference report {rc_hb1001_576}.

race_context: House District 84 is in Allen County and includes part of Fort Wayne and most of St. Joe Township, according to the House Republican caucus {caucus_morris}.
Morris was reelected unopposed in 2024 {wiki_2026}. Both nominees were unopposed in the May 5, 2026 primaries {wiki_2026}.

Key differences: Morris's legislative focus includes commerce and small business, and he joined other northeast Indiana legislators in highlighting a state utility-affordability review {caucus_morris} {caucus_iurc}; Meehan's campaign focuses on cost of living, housing, child care and corporate tax breaks {meehan_issues}.
No debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent since 2010 and chair of the House Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development Committee {caucus_morris}.
background: Small-business owner who has founded several ventures in the district; B.S. from Indiana University {caucus_morris}.

Former state-sworn reserve officer with the New Haven Police Department (2005–2006); serves on the boards of Purdue University Extension Service and Northeast Indiana Crime Stoppers, according to the caucus {caucus_morris}.
Moved to Fort Wayne in 1976 and graduated from Bishop Dwenger High School {caucus_morris}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Says of the death penalty: "I do not believe that another human being should be taking a human life" {caucus_hb1287}. Told 21Alive that if the law stands, "the same people who voted for it should fully understand what it means" {wpta_hb1287}.
Said the March 2026 IURC energy-affordability investigation, which included Indiana Michigan Power, "adds another layer of accountability" to HEA 1002 {caucus_iurc}.
On HEA 1424: "Farmers and small business owners work hard to provide quality products to their communities" {caucus_newlaws}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No public statements about his challenger were found.
plans: No 2026 campaign platform was found; his campaign domain points to his caucus page {morris_site}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were verified.
gaps: No campaign issue statements for 2026 were found.
Final status of HB 1287 was not confirmed; a search snippet suggested it did not advance.

candidates.summary: Misti Meehan is a small-business owner who says she has worked more than a decade with the Allen County Election Board {meehan_about}. She was unopposed in the Democratic primary {wiki_2026}.
background: Small-business owner; served in the Indiana Army National Guard {meehan_about}.
Says she has worked with the Allen County Election Board for over a decade {meehan_about}.
In 2019 she was chair of the Allen County Democratic Party and announced a run for the 1st District seat on the Fort Wayne City Council {wowo_2019}.
Attended Northrop High School and IPFW; says she was born and raised in the community {meehan_about}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Says "too many working people are struggling while large corporations receive tax breaks and special treatment" and that businesses must succeed "but not on the backs of Hoosier families" {meehan_issues} {meehan_site}.
Says "Families are being priced out of their own communities" {meehan_issues}.
Says "childcare has become unaffordable or unavailable for many" {meehan_issues}.

on_incumbent: No statements about Morris or his record were found on her website {meehan_site}.
plans: Says she wants "practical solutions that lower costs, strengthen our local economy" {meehan_issues} and to bring "practical, bipartisan leadership back to the Statehouse" {meehan_site}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were verified.
gaps: No news coverage of her 2026 campaign was found.
Her website offers no specific policy proposals.
Outcome of her 2019 city council bid not checked.
